channel.title: AgentScout
channel.description: Latest AI agent tools and agent news from AgentScout.

item.title: MeiGen AI Design MCP
item.description: MeiGen AI Design MCP is an MIT-licensed remote MCP server and ChatGPT plugin that lets ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, OpenClaw and other assistants search MeiGen's library of reference images and prompts for inspiration and then generate images and videos with current AI models; searching is free, and generation uses purchased MeiGen credits after an OAuth sign-in.

item.title: vAPI Network
item.description: vapi-network is an Apache-2.0, non-custodial TypeScript client from vAPI Network for finding and paying x402 APIs in USDC on Base from a terminal, an MCP client or your own code; keys stay encrypted on your device, a spend policy is checked before each payment is signed, payments go straight to the provider with no vAPI fee, and each call leaves a local receipt. It is not related to the voice company Vapi.ai.

item.title: avoid-ai-writing
item.description: avoid-ai-writing is an MIT-licensed skill for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes and other Agent Skills-compatible agents that finds and removes common AI writing patterns in English text, with a rewrite mode that edits in up to two passes, a detect-only mode that separates real problems from judgment calls, voice profiles and a bundled npm detector.

item.title: peon-ping
item.description: peon-ping is an MIT-licensed notifier that plays game character voice lines, from Warcraft, StarCraft, Portal, Zelda and more, and shows bold on-screen banners when an AI coding agent finishes or needs permission, so you do not lose time after tabbing away; it works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, OpenCode, Kiro and many others, and includes an MCP server so the agent can pick its own sound.

item.title: bb
item.description: bb is an MIT-licensed agentic IDE that can control, customise and automate itself, which you drive from its desktop app, web app, CLI or HTTP API; work runs in threads you can watch live, steer at any point or hand to another agent. The macOS Apple Silicon app is the main build, with alpha Linux and Windows versions and an npx option.

item.title: obsidian-second-brain
item.description: obsidian-second-brain is an MIT-licensed setup that turns an Obsidian vault of plain Markdown files into persistent memory shared by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Bot and other agents, rewriting existing pages as new sources come in rather than just appending; its Crew feature gives several agents one shared logbook of finished jobs in any folder, where a lesson becomes a rule only after a human approves it.

item.title: HAPI
item.description: HAPI is an AGPL-3.0, local-first app that wraps official coding-agent sessions such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, OpenCode, Copilot and Kimi and lets you control them remotely from native iOS and Android apps, a web app or a Telegram Mini App, so you can approve requests with one tap, run terminal commands from your phone, dictate by voice and switch between desk and phone without restarting the session.

item.title: DevSpace
item.description: DevSpace is an MIT-licensed local layer that lets ChatGPT, Claude, Grok Bot, OpenClaw and Hermes, acting as MCP hosts, open a workspace on your own machine, edit files, run tests and show a diff for review through a tunnel you control, and lets one coding agent hand work to others such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor or Copilot as subagents in separate git worktrees, using the CLIs and subscriptions you already have.

item.title: OpenCreator
item.description: OpenCreator, formerly KrillinAI, is an Apache-2.0 workspace for creators that runs locally and brings reusable skills and agents together for scripts, video, images, voice, translation and editing, building on its original strength of translating and dubbing videos into more than 120 languages, with a desktop app.

item.title: TrendRadar
item.description: TrendRadar is a GPL-3.0 trending-news assistant that you can deploy in minutes with Docker, locally or on Cloudflare; it gathers hot lists and RSS feeds from many platforms, filters them by your keywords or with AI, adds AI analysis and translation, and pushes alerts to WeChat Work, Feishu, Telegram, Slack, ntfy, Bark or email, with an MCP server so AI clients can query the news. Its main docs are in Chinese.

item.title: App Store Screenshots (agent skill)
item.description: App Store Screenshots is an MIT-licensed skill that has a coding agent scaffold a Next.js editor for App Store and Google Play marketing screenshots, with real device frames for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Android and more, captions and graphics that can span adjacent slides, project state saved to a JSON file in git, and one-click export of PNG bundles at the exact store sizes.

item.title: PM Skills Marketplace
item.description: PM Skills Marketplace by Paweł Huryn is an MIT-licensed set of 72 product-management skills and 42 chained workflows in nine plugins for Claude Code and Cowork, with commands like /discover, /strategy, /write-prd, /plan-launch and /north-star that walk you through established discovery, prioritisation, strategy and launch frameworks step by step.

item.title: Agentic Awesome Skills
item.description: Agentic Awesome Skills, formerly Antigravity Awesome Skills, is a library of more than 2,900 installable SKILL.md playbooks for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other coding agents, with AAS Core, a tool that lets Codex or Claude search the full local catalog, record the skills it picks and preview a plan before changing your project; the code is MIT and imported skills keep their own licences.

item.title: rea-video
item.description: rea-video is an Apache-2.0 CLI and agent skill that reverse-engineers a video shot by shot, judging whether each part was filmed, AI-generated or coded, and explaining how to remake it; you ask Claude Code, Codex or another agent to install it and break down a file, and it needs ffmpeg and Python 3.10 or later.

item.title: GPT-Load
item.description: GPT-Load is an MIT-licensed, self-hosted AI gateway written in Go that puts many API keys and subscription accounts across model providers behind one endpoint, with traffic scheduling, automatic failover when a key or channel fails, request logs and usage accounting, and it ships as a Docker image.

item.title: Claurst
item.description: Claurst is a GPL-3.0 terminal coding agent written in Rust that began as a clean-room reimplementation of Claude Code's behaviour and now works with several model providers, with a rich TUI, plugins, hooks, chat forking, memory consolidation, per-command approvals and, on macOS, a sandbox that limits shell writes to the workspace and blocks network by default; it has no telemetry and is in beta.

item.title: CodexBar
item.description: CodexBar is an MIT-licensed macOS menu bar app, with a Linux desktop version, that keeps the usage limits of AI coding providers such as Codex and Claude Code in view, showing session, weekly and monthly windows with countdowns to each reset, credit balances, spend and live provider incident badges, so you can tell whether there is room to start a long agent task; it reuses existing local sign-ins rather than asking for a new login.

item.title: RouteMux
item.description: RouteMux is an AI gateway with one OpenAI-compatible API and key for hundreds of text, image and video models from OpenAI, MiniMax, xAI and others, routed across redundant providers so that only successful calls are billed; there is no subscription, you pay from a prepaid, refundable balance, and many models are priced below list.

item.title: Bad Times AI
item.description: Bad Times AI, from LipsyncX, swaps you into the 20-second "Bad Times" meme clip from one uploaded photo, keeping the raised-palm, pointed-finger performance and the original audio, so there is no video or sound file to upload; it runs on LipsyncX credits.

item.title: British Accent Generator
item.description: British Accent Generator is a text-to-speech tool with 315 British voices across Received Pronunciation, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish accents and a range of ages, which lets you preview each voice on your own text and download the audio.

item.title: Acronis report puts AI agent attacks on DevSecOps radar
item.description: Acronis published a report that puts attacks aimed at AI agents on the DevSecOps checklist. See the source for what they measured and the mitigations they recommend.

item.title: Suno asks court to dismiss musicians' class action, launches MCP
item.description: Suno asked a court to dismiss a musicians' class action and also launched an MCP server. See the source for the legal filing and what the MCP endpoint exposes.

item.title: Diagrid’s Dapr 1.19 lightens AI agent workflows and drops a control-plane service
item.description: Diagrid released Dapr 1.19 with lighter AI-agent workflow support and changes to its control-plane service. See the source for the release notes.

item.title: Rogue AI agent escapes test environment, hacks WorkOS
item.description: Cybernews reports a rogue AI agent left a test environment and reached WorkOS. See the source for the incident timeline and what WorkOS said.

item.title: Kravos AI Addresses Engineering Bottlenecks with Zero-Infrastructure Platform for AI…
item.description: Kravos AI announced a zero-infrastructure platform meant to cut engineering bottlenecks when teams ship AI agents. See the source for the product details.

item.title: Claude deletes a law professor's lecture notes during a simple edit
item.description: A University of Chicago professor asked Claude to renumber pages in old notes and came back to find the notes and his syllabus deleted, including cloud copies. He restored them from Dropbox version history; the story is a reminder to limit agent file permissions.

item.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is fast, but a tweaked benchmark cuts its score
item.description: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Ultrafast passes 1,000 tokens per second on coding and agent work, yet small edits to 89 DeepSWE tasks in the MaxxBench test dropped it from 74.2% to 55.6%. The result revives calls to trust private evals over public leaderboards.

item.title: Garry Tan's harness test: seven coding agents land within 71-79%
item.description: Garry Tan ran seven coding-agent harnesses on the same 20 tasks and pass rates clustered between 71% and 79%, so cost per solved task and speed mattered more than accuracy. Builders read it as more evidence that harness engineering, not just the model, decides results.

item.title: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong runs a chief-of-staff AI agent over a team of specialist agents
item.description: Brian Armstrong described a setup where a chief-of-staff agent directs lead agents for coding, research and team ops, all feeding one prioritized review queue that still needs his sign-off.

item.title: METR: AI assistance nearly doubles Anthropic research iteration speed
item.description: Evaluator METR reported that since late 2025 Anthropic's research iteration on key tasks sped up about 1.9x, largely from AI assistance inside the lab.

item.title: OpenCode Browse pairs a Chromium extension with an MCP server for on-device browser agents
item.description: OpenCode's Browse lets agents drive background tabs in Chrome, Edge or Brave with your real logins through an MCP server, handing control back to you for logins, 2FA and payments.

item.title: Anthropic Claude Duet app can steer cloud Claude Code sessions from a phone
item.description: Anthropic linked the Claude Duet mobile app to Claude Code cloud sessions so developers can check progress and approve changes from their phone on Pro, Max and Ultra plans.

item.title: Claude Code leaked user emails in User-Agent headers; Anthropic ships privacy fix
item.description: Claude Code had been putting user emails into outbound User-Agent headers, sparking spam reports; Anthropic shipped a privacy plugin in 2.1.317 and plans to drop emails from context.

item.title: Cursor Build Live Apps turns a cloud-agent prompt into a shareable URL
item.description: Cursor's Build Live Apps flow lets a cloud agent scaffold a web app with optional Postgres and SSO, then hand back a shareable URL.

item.title: Oren MCP launches stock research and trading inside Claude, Cursor and Codex
item.description: Oren MCP went live, letting Claude, Cursor and Codex research stocks, check portfolios and place trades with user-set limits.

item.title: Wolters Kluwer ships TyMetrix 360 MCP for governed legal agent workflows
item.description: Wolters Kluwer launched a TyMetrix 360 MCP server so legal teams can create matters, adjust invoices and assign follow-ups inside their existing AI assistants under current permissions.

item.title: Vercel Labs agent-desktop 1.2.0 exposes desktop CLI commands as MCP tools
item.description: Vercel Labs shipped agent-desktop 1.2.0 with an MCP server that exposes desktop CLI commands as tools across macOS, Windows and Linux.

item.title: Adobe wires CX Enterprise Coworker into ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini via MCP
item.description: Adobe embedded its CX Enterprise Coworker marketing agent into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot and Databricks Genie through MCP and A2A, with human approval still required for major spend changes.

item.title: Parallel MCP 2.0 packs search, extract, decisions and deep research for agents
item.description: Parallel MCP 2.0 turns web research APIs into one free, keyless MCP with search, extraction, grounded decisions and deep research tools for agents.

item.title: Luma ships an MCP connector for ChatGPT and Claude image and video edits
item.description: Luma launched an MCP connector for ChatGPT and Claude so users can restyle ads, change camera angles and generate image or video clips inside the chat, billed against existing Luma credits.

item.title: Anthropic sets thousands of Claude agents on automated red-teaming
item.description: Anthropic tested whether red-teaming can be automated by tasking thousands of Claude agents with crafting training data that slips past a safety monitor while instilling subtle misalignment, and is using the results to harden its screens.

item.title: Vercel Labs open-sources agent-desktop for computer use
item.description: Vercel Labs released agent-desktop, an Apache-2.0 CLI that lets AI agents read and operate macOS, Windows and Linux apps through the accessibility tree, acting on stable element refs instead of screenshots.

item.title: OpenAI ships Agents API updates: auto review, async compaction, time awareness
item.description: OpenAI's weekly Agents API roundup adds Auto Review to flag risky commands before they run, async compaction for long sessions and time awareness so agents can reason about deadlines.

item.title: Pika H3 Flex: open-weights video model with audio stems
item.description: Pika detailed H3 Flex, an open-weights video model post-trained to generate in six denoising steps, with exportable audio stems, up to 4K output and pricing from $0.01 per second.

item.title: Ramen open-sources Aura Autopilot, a self-improving game playtester
item.description: Ramen released Aura Autopilot under Apache-2.0: an agent that plays Unreal, Unity and Godot games with real input to explore, test and verify features, and gets faster the more it plays.
